reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) shows Al-Ni driven clustering and a clustering-to-ordering transition under compressive strain in Al0.1CrCoFeNi, supporting the first and third premises. However, the evidence does not directly address whether this LCO stabilizes the microstructure against phase transformations, nor does it compare compressive versus tensile loading or extend to nanoalloys specifically, leaving the second, fourth, and fifth premises unsupported.
premises: Al-Ni attractive interactions drive local chemical ordering (LCO) in Al0.1CrCoFeNi
LCO creates a stronger bonding network that stabilizes the microstructure
Compressive stress promotes LCO, while tensile stress does not
Enhanced LCO retards phase transformations at high temperatures
The proposed mechanism applies to nanoalloys of similar composition under near-melting conditions
